chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abi 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Aba Ibrahim عليه السلام, “At what time is it more beloved to you that we depart from Jam'?” He said, “A little before the sun rises; that is the most beloved of times to me.” I said, “If we remain until the sun rises?” He said, “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Musa al-Kazim عليه السلام, the Imam being asked about the ruling
key_terms.أَحَبُّ السَّاعَاتِ إِلَيَّ: the most preferred time in this context
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', referring to al-Muzdalifah/al-Mash'ar during hajj
key_terms.سَاعَةٍ: a specific time or hour being asked about
key_terms.قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ بِقَلِيلٍ: a little before sunrise, identified as the preferred time
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.نُفِيضَ: to depart in procession or move onward from a ritual station

ai.seo_question: When is the recommended time to depart from Jam' during hajj, and is it permissible to remain until sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith states the preferred time for departing from Jam' (al-Mash'ar al-Haram) during hajj: shortly before sunrise. It also clarifies that remaining until sunrise is permissible and carries no harm, indicating a recommended time rather than an obligatory limit.
